summary: Modernization platform shows good architectural patterns but faces critical security risks from legacy VB6 code patterns. Strong foundation with comprehensive schemas and modular design, but requires immediate attention to SQL injection vulnerabilities and data migration strategy.

hotspots.reason: SQL injection vulnerabilities in string concatenated queries

provenance.evidence: WHERE AccountNo=" & txtAccountNo.Text - direct user input concatenation

hotspots.reason: No clear migration path from VB6 ADO to modern database access

provenance.evidence: VB6 Recordset pattern requires complete rewrite for C# modernization

hotspots.reason: No visible authentication or authorization mechanisms

provenance.evidence: No auth-related modules or configurations detected in 304 scanned files

risks.title: Critical SQL Injection Vulnerability
risks.description: Legacy VB6 code uses direct string concatenation for SQL queries, allowing arbitrary SQL execution through user input fields

risks.title: Data Contract Preservation Risk
risks.description: Migration from VB6 ADO Recordset to C# may introduce behavioral changes in balance calculations and transaction handling

risks.title: Banking Compliance Gap
risks.description: No visible audit trails, transaction logging, or compliance controls for financial operations

risks.title: Concurrent Access Control
risks.description: Legacy code shows no concurrency control for balance updates, risking race conditions in multi-user scenarios
